tier_reason: Upgraded D->C: the listed changelog (gevent 1.3b1 Enhancements) has the no-numbers sentence verbatim, but the PR it cites, gevent PR #1088, has the gevent maintainer's timing tables for the gevent dnspython resolver against the gevent c-ares resolver, and the benchmark code is public (gevent benchmarks/bench_dns_resolver.py). It is not A: no CPU model, compiler or flags are given, only 'my macOS machine' and a local dnsmasq cache. It is not B: these are the integrator's own numbers, not peer-reviewed and not from an independent suite.

corrections.claimed_speedup: gevent PR #1088 (gevent maintainer, local caching dnsmasq, macOS): 300 sequential gethostbyname calls took c-ares 3.19-3.60 s vs dnspython 0.81-1.80 s across PyPy 2 5.10 / CPython 2.7 / 3.6 / 3.7b1 (about 2-4.4x, derived from page data). 100 parallel greenlet lookups took c-ares 2.33-2.60 s vs dnspython 0.18-0.29 s (about 8.6-13x, derived from page data). bench_dns_resolver.py on CPython 3.7.0: dnspython 147 us vs ares 6.56 ms sequential, 152 us vs 6.76 ms parallel (about 44-45x, derived from page data). The changelog says only 'generally faster than c-ares', and the gevent dnspython resolver docstring says 'usually much faster than the c-ares resolver'. CONTESTED: another user on the same PR, running the same script on Linux Mint 19.1 / CPython 2.7.15, got ares at 36.7 us vs dnspython at 100 us sequential (ares about 2.7x faster, derived from page data).
corrections.workload: gevent resolver backends (gevent.resolver.dnspython vs gevent.resolver.ares) doing gethostbyname against a local dnsmasq configured to cache everything: 300 sequential lookups, 100 concurrent greenlet lookups, and gevent benchmarks/bench_dns_resolver.py (pyperf, N=150, RUN_COUNT=2)
corrections.hardware: unspecified macOS machine (gevent maintainer); counter-measurement on unspecified Linux Mint 19.1 machine; no CPU models stated
corrections.caveats: Numbers come from gevent's maintainer (gevent PR #1088), not from the dnspython project. They compare gevent's resolver wrappers: dnspython (pure Python, with its own TTL cache) vs c-ares behind gevent's Cython binding, so they do not test dnspython against c-ares as a standalone library. The gevent PR author found early runs against 8.8.8.8 'wildly variable and extremely suspect', and in that setup dnspython was about 3x slower than c-ares. Only the later runs against a local caching dnsmasq favour dnspython. An independent rerun of the same benchmark script on Linux (gevent 1.3.7, Python 2.7) found c-ares about 2.7x faster than dnspython, so the win looks platform- and setup-dependent (macOS). No CPU model, compiler or flags are given. gevent labels its dnspython resolver 'experimental', and it does not read /etc/hosts. dnspython's GitHub license shows NOASSERTION, but the LICENSE file holds two ISC-style notices (Dnspython Contributors; Nominum/Google).
